briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Regulators Crack Down on Bad Actors as National Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan's Cannabis Regulatory Agency kept its crackdown going this week — revoking licenses over fake product and illegal influencer deals, while a court found a marijuana farm illegally filled protected wetlands — even as GOP gubernatorial hopeful John James keeps courting industry cash with a tax-repeal pledge. Nationally, Tilray posted record quarterly revenue, New York topped $4 billion in lifetime legal sales, and the FDA opened the door to ibogaine research while a new study points to psilocybin-related compounds helping treat postpartum depression.

local.text: Michigan revokes 20 grower licenses over fake flower — The Cannabis Regulatory Agency pulled 20 Class C licenses from GP Holdings LLC (dba Millie Montana Industries) of Clare and fined it $2 million after packages labeled marijuana flower tested as dirt and mulch with no THC.

State finalizes $251,250 fine over influencer vape cartridges — The CRA issued a final order revoking the retail license of Budbridge LLC (dba Muha Meds Ypsilanti) for seven rule violations, including illegally handing out vape cartridges to social media influencers.

Court finds marijuana farm illegally filled protected wetlands — A 30th Circuit Court judge ruled Bliss Corporate, Inc. cleared, dredged and filled 15.9 acres of wetlands in Sherman Township to build a cannabis farm, with penalties to be decided next month.

John James leans on cannabis donors for tax-repeal campaign — The GOP governor hopeful has raised roughly $1.2 million since late July, including nearly $90,000 from a fundraiser hosted by JARS Cannabis executives, while pledging to repeal or cut the 24% wholesale tax.

Fawn River recalls dab product over banned chemical — The company voluntarily recalled its Hash Melts (Green Crack 1G Live Rosin Dab), produced June 16, 2026, after state testing found a banned chemical in the product.

national.text: Tilray posts record quarterly revenue — The company reported first-quarter fiscal-2027 net revenue of $257 million, up 23% year-over-year, with gross margin expanding to about 30% and its beverage unit, including BrewDog, turning profitable.

FDA opens door to ibogaine research for opioid use disorder — The agency announced a formal Request for Information on designing early-phase ibogaine clinical trials for opioid use disorder and PTSD, accepting public comment through Nov. 20, 2026.

New York tops $4 billion in lifetime legal cannabis sales — State regulators disclosed licensed dispensaries generated $512.6 million in third-quarter 2026 sales, pushing year-to-date sales to $1.41 billion and lifetime adult-use sales past $4 billion since 2022.

States press DEA for rescheduling implementation guidance — Regulators including California's Department of Cannabis Control are seeking clarity from the DEA after its chief administrative law judge stayed the broader rescheduling hearing pending a GAO report, with responses due Oct. 13.

Study points to psilocybin-related compound for postpartum depression — New research reported this week found luvesilocin, a mushroom-derived psilocybin-related compound, may hold promise as a treatment for postpartum depression.
